newsitem.title: GREECE: Athens bourse's operational risk fell in '96- IFC.
newsitem.headline: Athens bourse's operational risk fell in '96- IFC.

text.p: Athens bourse's aggregate operational efficiency improved in 1996, but still ranked 10th among 15 emerging markets according to figures in the 1997 emerging bourses factbook published by the IFC.

Figures which reflect service levels received by global custodians and passed along to their institutional clients showed that the Athens stock exchange ranked 11th among 15 emerging markets in safekeeping and settlement efficiency.

The ratings were based on safekeeping, settlement and operational risk benchmark indexes prepared by the Global Securities Consulting Services (GSCS), the International Financial Corporation (IFC) said.
Portugal ranked first in safekeeping and operational efficiency followed by Korea and Turkey. Turkey was rated first in settlement procedures followed by Brazil and Portugal.
India ranked last in settlement and operational efficiency in 1996 and Peru occupied the last place in safekeeping, it added.

The safekeeping benchmark index measures the overall cost of failed trades to market participants and reflects average trade size, local market interest rates, the proportion of trades that fail and the length of time for which they fail, it said.
The settlement benchmark index measures efficiency in dividend and interest collection, reclamation of excess withheld taxes and rights protection in the event of corporate action.

Market yields on equity and bonds, withholding taxes and reclaim potential, average time between payment date and receipt of payment, local interest rates and the number and type of corporate actions that occur are included in the settlement index.
The operational risk benchmark index takes into account both the settlement and safekeeping indexes assigning them a different weight depending on the complexity of each market, it said.
The risk-reward ratio in emerging markets is calculated without regard to the unexpected costs of failure in market processes. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
